step1_figure.circuit_type: Two-stage CMOS Operational Amplifier with Cascode Current Biasing and RC Pole-Splitting Compensation
step1_figure.description: Figure 24.8 depicts the two-stage op-amp schematic comprising an NMOS differential input pair (M1, M2), PMOS current mirror load (M3, M4), NMOS cascode tail current source (M6T, M6B), PMOS common-source second stage (M7), and NMOS cascode sink load (M8T, M8B) with compensation network Rz-Cc and load cap CL. Figure 24.9 depicts the open-loop AC test configuration with a 100 MEG resistor and 10 uF capacitor providing DC bias feedback while isolating AC feedback.

dc_open_loop_gain.description: Low-frequency open-loop voltage gain of the two-stage operational amplifier

equation.explanation: Product of the first-stage gain (gm1*R1) and second-stage common-source gain (gm2*R2), where R1 is the resistance at node 1 (ro2 || ro4) and R2 is the output resistance (ro7 || ro_cascode).

sky130_expected.calculation: For I_D1 = 10 uA, Vov ≈ 0.15 V: gm1 = 2*ID1/Vov ≈ 133 uA/V. ro2 || ro4 ≈ 1 / ((lambda_n + lambda_p)*ID1) = 1 / (0.2 * 10u) = 500 kΩ. Stage 1 gain A1 ≈ 133u * 500k = 66.5 (36.5 dB). For stage 2, I_D7 ≈ 10 uA, gm2 ≈ 133 uA/V, R2 ≈ ro7 = 1 / (0.1 * 10u) = 1.0 MΩ. Stage 2 gain A2 ≈ 133u * 1M = 133 (42.5 dB). Total gain AOL = 66.5 * 133 ≈ 8844 ≈ 78.9 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: In 130 nm CMOS at VDD=1.8V, intrinsic transistor gain gm*ro is typically between 30 and 100 per stage, yielding 60 dB to 85 dB for two stages.

unity_gain_frequency.description: Frequency at which the magnitude of open-loop gain drops to 0 dB (unity)

equation.explanation: The unity-gain frequency (gain-bandwidth product) set by the input stage transconductance gm1 and the Miller compensation capacitor Cc.
equation.assumptions: Dominant pole approximation holds, f_un << f_p2, RHP zero is eliminated or pushed out.

sky130_expected.calculation: With gm1 ≈ 150 uA/V and Cc = 2.4 pF: f_un = 150e-6 / (2 * pi * 2.4e-12) ≈ 9.95 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Equation (24.10) directly designs for fun = 10 MHz with Cc = 2.4 pF and gm1 = 150 uA/V.

dominant_pole_frequency.description: -3 dB cutoff frequency of the open-loop response due to Miller compensation at node 1

equation.explanation: Dominant low-frequency pole formed by Miller multiplication of compensation capacitor Cc.
equation.assumptions: Miller effect dominates node 1 capacitance; gm2*R2 >> 1.

sky130_expected.reasoning: With open-loop gain around 75 dB (~5600) and unity-gain frequency at 10 MHz, f1 = fun / AOL ≈ 10 MHz / 5600 ≈ 1.8 kHz.

second_pole_frequency.description: Non-dominant pole frequency associated with the output node (node 2)

equation.explanation: Pole pushed to high frequency due to pole-splitting by Cc.

sky130_expected.reasoning: As shown on page 779, f2 evaluates near 210 MHz when Cc and CL are on the order of 100 fF to a few pF.

phase_margin.description: Phase difference from -180 degrees at the unity-gain frequency

equation.explanation: Stability measure indicating damping and settling behavior in negative feedback.
equation.assumptions: Single feedback loop with unity feedback factor beta = 1.

sky130_expected.calculation: At fun ≈ 10 MHz, dominant pole contributes -90°. Second pole f2 ≈ 200 MHz contributes -arctan(10/200) = -2.9°. With zero cancelled by Rz, phase ≈ -93°, giving PM = 180° - 93° ≈ 87°.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The textbook designs the compensated amplifier to achieve approximately 90 degrees of phase margin.

gain_margin.description: Gain attenuation below 0 dB at the frequency where phase shift reaches -180 degrees

equation.explanation: Amount of additional loop gain before instability occurs.

sky130_expected.calculation: Phase reaches -180° well beyond 200 MHz, where gain is far below 0 dB (attenuated by ~20 to 30 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Page 781 states the gain margin is approximately 25 dB for this compensated op-amp.

power_dissipation.description: Total quiescent power consumed by the operational amplifier

equation.formula: P = VDD * sum(I_bias) = VDD * (I_M6 + I_M8 + I_bias_circuit)
equation.explanation: Static power dissipation calculated from the sum of DC currents supplied from VDD.
equation.assumptions: No external DC resistive load connected to vout.

sky130_expected.calculation: VDD = 1.8 V. I_M6 = 20 uA (diff-amp tail), I_M8 = 10 uA (second stage), I_bias ≈ 30 uA for the wide-swing bias network SUB_1. Total current ≈ 60 uA. P = 1.8 V * 60 uA = 108 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The core op-amp burns (20u + 10u)*1.8V = 54 uW, and the bias generator adds roughly an equal amount.

output_swing_max.description: Maximum output voltage before the output PMOS (M7) enters triode

equation.explanation: Upper saturation limit set by PMOS M7 overdrive voltage Vov7.

sky130_expected.calculation: VDD = 1.8 V. With V_SD,sat ≈ 0.15 V, V_out,max = 1.8 - 0.15 = 1.65 V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: PMOS M7 requires at least ~100-150 mV overdrive to remain in saturation.

output_swing_min.description: Minimum output voltage before the cascode current sink (M8T, M8B) enters triode

equation.explanation: Lower limit set by the compliance voltage of the wide-swing NMOS cascode current sink.

sky130_expected.calculation: For wide-swing cascode biased sink: V_DS,sat ≈ 100 mV each, V_out,min ≈ 200 mV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Wide-swing cascode maintains saturation down to approximately 2*Vdsat.

max_sink_current.description: Maximum current the op-amp output stage can sink from a load

equation.explanation: Sinking current is limited by the constant current sink M8 (M8T/M8B).

sky130_expected.calculation: M8 is sized for 10 uA constant current sink. Hence I_sink,max = 10 uA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The second stage pull-down is a constant current source of nominal 10 uA.

step3_testbench.description: Comprehensive ngspice testbench for Baker Chapter 24 Two-Stage CMOS Op-Amp measuring DC operating point, power, open-loop frequency response (gain, unity-gain frequency, phase margin, gain margin), output swing, and transient step response.
